concern_details.detail: main data entities stored and their relationships
concern_details.why: The seven persisted entities listed in persistence.xml (User, Citizen, MunicipalOperator, Report, InternalNote, StatusUpdate, Notification) and the two embeddables are drawn. The associations and multiplicities match the JPA mappings: citizen_id NOT NULL gives 1, operator_id nullable gives 0..1, and the StatusUpdate and InternalNote operator_id columns are NOT NULL. Two things a database engineer needs are not on the diagram. Only 'users' and 'reports' are named as tables; status_updates, internal_notes and notifications are not. None of the FK columns (citizen_id, operator_id, report_id) is named, although the legend says the arrows stand for foreign keys.

concern_details.detail: information persisted throughout the lifecycle of a report
concern_details.why: The view shows the attributes that hold lifecycle data (currentStatusName, citizenEditable, operator, StatusUpdate rows, notes, notifications). It does not show the lifecycle itself. In the code, the status strings go submitted -> assigned -> in_progress -> resolved. Report.updateStatus writes a StatusUpdate on every change. The operator is set on the report when its status is updated (ReportService.updateReportStatus calls assignOperator). citizenEditable is true only while the status is submitted. Notifications are created only for 'assigned' and 'resolved' (Notification.isStatusNotifiable) and are saved separately, without cascade. The note names the Java state classes (Submitted, InProgress...) instead of the stored values ('in_progress'), and the README wrongly gives 'in progress'. Nothing says that currentStatusName, StatusUpdate.newStatus and Notification.notifiedStatus share one value domain.

concern_details.detail: how users, reports, locations, categories, states, state changes, internal notes and notifications are related
concern_details.why: Users, reports, locations, state changes, notes and notifications are related correctly. Categories appear only as an attribute plus a note listing the values, not as an enumeration that Report uses. States appear only as a String attribute and a note, so it is not visible that StatusUpdate.newStatus and Notification.notifiedStatus hold the same status values as Report.currentStatusName.

concern_details.detail: which parts of the application depend on the persisted information
concern_details.why: ReportService, UserService and PersistenceService are drawn, and notes list the controllers that use the services (8 and 7, both checked against Control/). No dependency is drawn from the services to the entities. Only service -> PersistenceService appears, so the reader cannot tell which service reads or writes which entity. ReportService uses Report, StatusUpdate, InternalNote, Notification, MunicipalOperator and User. UserService uses User, Citizen and MunicipalOperator. The services also query by attribute-path strings such as findByFields(..., "report.reportId"), so renaming a mapped attribute breaks them. A database engineer needs that coupling. The schema is generated by hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto in persistence.xml, which is mentioned only in the README.

level_why: Entity attributes with PK, length and unique constraints, embedded types and multiplicities are the right depth for a database engineer. Showing the services as a single dependent layer, with the controllers in notes, also fits. The view is slightly too abstract in two places: table and FK column names, and the stored state values with their transition and notification rules. The service operations add little unless they are tied to the entities they touch. Nothing needs to be dropped.
unsupported: Report note: 'The ReportStatus state objects (Submitted, Assigned, InProgress, Resolved)' are rebuilt from currentStatusName. That is true, but the values actually stored are 'submitted', 'assigned', 'in_progress', 'resolved' (Report.java STATUS_* constants), and the README calls one of them 'in progress'.
Legend 'Open arrow: foreign key': the arrows do match @ManyToOne join columns in the code, but the diagram names no FK columns, so the reader cannot check this from the view.
missing: Dependencies from ReportService to Report, StatusUpdate, InternalNote, Notification and MunicipalOperator/User, and from UserService to User, Citizen and MunicipalOperator, including the attribute-path queries (e.g. 'report.reportId' in ReportService.retrieveDetailsReport).

Report status lifecycle as stored values: submitted -> assigned -> in_progress -> resolved (Submitted/Assigned/InProgress/Resolved.updateStatus); citizenEditable is true only in 'submitted'; the operator is assigned on the status update; a StatusUpdate row is written per change.

Notification rules: created only for 'assigned' or 'resolved' (Notification.isStatusNotifiable); saved explicitly by ReportService.generateStatusChangeNotification; not cascaded from Report, so the notifications.report_id FK blocks deleting a report.

Table names status_updates, internal_notes and notifications, plus the FK columns citizen_id, operator_id and report_id with their NOT NULL settings. User is abstract (User.java) but is not marked abstract.
Schema generated by hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto, with no migration scripts (persistence.xml). This is relevant to anyone changing the persistence layer.
uml: User is abstract in the code but is drawn as a concrete class. Mark it {abstract} or use an italic name.
ReportCategory should be an «enumeration» class with its five literals, used as the type of Report.category, instead of a free-text constraint '{enum, 5 values}' plus a note.
Location and Credentials are value types (JPA @Embeddable) and should carry the standard «dataType» keyword. Location's attributes have no types (String).

Non-standard stereotypes «accent», «alert» and «muted» are in the source (hidden in the render). Constraints such as {≤ 50}, {discriminator} and {enum, 5 values} are informal. Prefer {PK}/{unique} style constraints or a note.
The legend recasts navigable association arrows as 'foreign key', which mixes ER and UML semantics. Either name the FK columns as role/constraint text or drop that claim.
fixes: Add «use» dependencies from ReportService and UserService to the specific entities they read or write, and note that queries depend on attribute paths (findByFields with 'report.reportId').

Show the report lifecycle as stored data: list the status values submitted/assigned/in_progress/resolved and their order, the rule that citizenEditable is true only in submitted, the rule that the operator is set on a status update, and the rule that notifications go out only for assigned and resolved. Use a note or a «enumeration»-style value list shared by currentStatusName, newStatus and notifiedStatus.

Name every table and FK column (status_updates, internal_notes, notifications; citizen_id, operator_id, report_id, with NOT NULL). State that Notification is not cascaded and its FK blocks report deletion.
Make ReportCategory an «enumeration» class, mark User {abstract}, mark Location and Credentials «dataType», and give Location's attributes types.
Remove the non-standard stereotypes and the 'open arrow = foreign key' legend line. Fix the README's 'in progress' to 'in_progress' and mention schema generation via hbm2ddl.auto.
